author: Stephen Wisnefski
title: Dow Jones Today: Stocks Plunge, Treasury Yields Surge as Investors Monitor Tax Bill; Dow Drops 800 Points, Bitcoin Wavers After Hitting Record High - Investopedia
description: Stocks tumbled and Treasury yields soared on Wednesday as investors kept close tabs on a sweeping tax and spending bill that's moving through Congress and could dramatically increase the federal deficit.
content_summary: On May 21, 2025, the stock market saw a major selloff with the Dow Jones Industrial Average plunging more than 800 points (1.9%) as investors reacted to growing concerns over a sweeping tax and spending bill moving through Congress. The bill is expected to significantly boost the federal deficit, causing Treasury yields to soar, with the 10-year Treasury note yield hitting 4.60%, the highest since February. Technology stocks were broadly lower, though Alphabet bucked the trend with a nearly 3% gain fueled by optimism around AI prospects revealed at its recent Google I/O conference. Bitcoin hit an all-time high of $109,900 before retreating to around $106,000. Safety assets like gold futures rose 1.2%. The market atmosphere remains fragile as macroeconomic concerns, regulatory scrutiny of major companies, and ongoing geopolitical risks persist.

author: Kevin Collier
title: Trump's crypto dinner cost over $1 million per seat, on average - NBC News
description: More than 200 wealthy, mostly anonymous crypto buyers are coming to Washington to have dinner with President Donald Trump.
content_summary: More than 200 cryptocurrency investors, many anonymous and foreign nationals, paid between $55,000 and $37.7 million each to attend a dinner with former President Donald Trump, held at Trump National Golf Club in Washington, D.C. The $TRUMP token contests secured seats, with total spending across winners amounting to $394 million. Analysts raised concerns about foreign nationals buying political influence through cryptocurrency donations, which is illegal under U.S. law. The dinner illuminates ongoing controversies about Trump’s use of office for personal financial gain and the opaque intersection of cryptocurrency and political fundraising. The event also exemplifies broader regulatory challenges fitting blockchain-based assets into traditional campaign finance frameworks.

author: Bertha Coombs
title: Cigna announces new deal for copay caps on Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk weight loss drugs - CNBC
description: Cigna's pharmacy benefits unit Evernorth said the deal will bring prices down for employers and their workers.
content_summary: Cigna's pharmacy benefits unit Evernorth reached a new coverage deal with drugmakers Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk to cap out-of-pocket costs for GLP-1 weight loss drugs Wegovy and Zepbound at $200 monthly for insured patients. This initiative aims to encourage wider employer coverage of these costly medications, addressing affordability barriers. The deal includes a simplified pre-authorization process and consistent pricing across retail and home delivery pharmacies. Large employers and insurers are gradually negotiating discounts estimated between 30% to 50% off list prices. The move precedes Medicare discount negotiations set for 2027 and responds to growing demand for effective obesity treatments amid rising health concerns and insurer hesitancy due to high drug costs.

author: Gabrielle Fonrouge
title: Nike will raise prices on a wide range of products as soon as this week - CNBC
description: Nike is raising prices on a range of merchandise as it braces for tariffs to hit its profits and tries to carry out a turnaround.
content_summary: Nike announced price increases across various adult footwear, apparel, and equipment by $2 to $10, anticipated on shelves as early as this week, effective June 1, 2025. Footwear priced between $100 and $150 will rise by $5, and higher-priced sneakers by $10. Notably, children's products and Nike's Air Force 1 shoes will not be affected. The hikes are attributed to ongoing tariffs on imports from China and Vietnam, which impact Nike's manufacturing costs. Although the company did not directly link the price changes to tariffs, the retail sector braces for margin pressure amid these levies. Nike's strategic pricing adjustments reflect efforts to maintain profitability while navigating cost and supply chain challenges.

author: Cora Lewis
title: Why are more shoppers struggling to repay 'buy now, pay later' loans? - Yahoo Finance
description: More Klarna customers are having trouble repaying their buy now, pay later loans, the short-term lender said this week.
content_summary: Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) services like Klarna are facing a rise in repayment struggles among users, an issue compounded by increased consumer debt levels and economic pressure on vulnerable segments. Klarna reported a 17% increase in first-quarter consumer credit losses, mainly due to a higher volume of loans issued. BNPL plans, often marketed as zero-interest and without credit checks, remain popular for their ease and flexibility, especially among younger populations and minority groups. However, increased late payments and missed installments raise concerns about overextension and financial instability. Regulatory oversight has lessened under the current administration, removing protections established to shield consumers from potential pitfalls, sparking calls for renewed attention to these growing risks.
